title: Pure lisse relative affine-curve step
statement:
Fix the coefficient and weight conventions of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be a
smooth separated morphism
between separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, with every nonempty geometric fiber a smooth affine
curve. Let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf that is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$.
Then for every $i$, $R^ih_!\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights
at most $w+i$.

proof.text: Fix a cohomological degree $i$ and put $\mathcal G_i=R^ih_!\mathcal F$. Apply [lem-zl-relative-curve-mixedness] to the given $h$ and $\mathcal F$: the base and source are separated and of finite type over the fixed finite field, $h$ is smooth and separated, every nonempty geometric fiber is a smooth affine curve, and $\mathcal F$ is lisse and punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, exactly as required there. Obtain a real number $u_i$ for which $\mathcal G_i$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u_i$. In particular it is a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf and has a finite filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves with punctually pure quotients; these are part of the meaning of mixedness in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. No lissity of $\mathcal G_i$ is asserted.

source.place: Proof: the curve-reduction lemma supplies a finite mixed filtration

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-relative-curve-punctual] to the same morphism and pure lisse sheaf. For every closed point $y$ of degree $m$, each local Frobenius eigenvalue $\alpha$ on $(\mathcal G_i)_{\bar y}$ satisfies $|\iota(\alpha)|\le(q^m)^{(w+i)/2}=q_y^{(w+i)/2}$, with $q_y=\#\kappa(y)=q^m$. Thus the punctual upper bound holds for the very same sheaf $\mathcal G_i$ shown mixed in step 1, with the same geometric-Frobenius and coefficient conventions.

source.place: Proof: first sentence, the punctual eigenvalue bound

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-mixed-punctual-cutoff] with $Y_0$ the given base, $\mathcal G=\mathcal G_i$, $u=u_i$, and $v=w+i$. Its constructibility and finite mixed-filtration hypothesis are supplied by step 1; its bound at every closed point is supplied by step 2. The base is separated and finite type, and the finite field, embedding $\iota$, coefficient field and local Frobenius operators agree throughout. The conclusion is that $R^ih_!\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+i$. Since $i$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion in every degree. The cutoff is applied to an existing filtration by Weil subsheaves, so no gluing of stalkwise filtrations is used.

source.place: Proof: apply the punctual cutoff with v=w+i; final sentence

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, expanded into three steps; the blueprint proof is agent-written
